summary.plain: ATLAS reported a new particle with a measured mass of about 126 GeV, presented with CMS at a CERN seminar on 4 July 2012. The collaboration's title calls it 'a new particle' in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson; its abstract says the observation is compatible with the production and decay of the Standard Model Higgs boson.
summary.technical: Combined search: H → ZZ(*) → 4ℓ, γγ and WW(*) → eνμν in 8 TeV data (about 5.8 fb⁻¹) combined with 7 TeV results (about 4.8 fb⁻¹: ZZ(*), WW(*), bb̄, τ⁺τ⁻, plus improved ZZ(*) → 4ℓ and γγ analyses). 'Clear evidence for the production of a neutral boson with a measured mass of 126.0 ± 0.4 (stat) ± 0.4 (sys) GeV is presented'; the observation has a local significance of 5.9σ (background fluctuation probability 1.7×10⁻⁹) and is compatible with the production and decay of the Standard Model Higgs boson.

title: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson with the ATLAS detector at the LHC
why_it_matters: The paper's introduction notes that the mechanism that breaks electroweak symmetry in the Standard Model, which gives mass to massive elementary particles, implies a scalar particle, the Higgs boson, and had not been verified experimentally. ATLAS reports clear evidence for a new neutral boson of mass 126.0 GeV whose observation is compatible with the production and decay of the Standard Model Higgs boson.
